testName: IISER IAT - Electrostatics: Advanced & Unique Problems (20 Questions)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A charge q is placed at the center of a neutral conducting spherical shell of inner radius a and outer radius b. The potential of the shell is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: By electrostatic induction, -q appears on inner surface (r = a) and +q on outer surface (r = b).
Step 2: The shell is an equipotential. Potential at any point inside conductor (including outer surface) is due to all charges: center q, inner surface -q, and outer surface +q.
Step 3: Potential at r = b: V = (1/4πε₀)[q/b (from center) + (-q)/b (from inner surface, at distance b) + q/b (from outer surface)] = q/(4πε₀b).
Step 4: The -q and +q on surfaces cancel their contributions at external points, leaving only the effective external charge q at center.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two point charges +q and -q are placed at (0,0,d) and (0,0,-d) respectively. The electric field at point (x,0,0) on the x-axis is directed:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: This is an electric dipole oriented along z-axis.
Step 2: At equatorial point (perpendicular bisector), the field is anti-parallel to dipole moment.
Step 3: Dipole moment p = q(2d) in +z direction. Field at equatorial point is opposite to p, so in -z direction.
Step 4: Wait, let me verify with calculation. Field from +q at (0,0,d): points from charge to point, has -z component. Field from -q at (0,0,-d): points toward charge, has -z component. Both add in -z direction. So answer is D (-z).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A uniformly charged disk of radius R has surface charge density σ. The electric field at distance z along axis is E = (σ/2ε₀)[1 - z/√(z²+R²)]. For z >> R, this reduces to:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: For z >> R: z/√(z²+R²) = z/(z√(1+R²/z²)) ≈ 1/(1 + R²/2z²) ≈ 1 - R²/2z².
Step 2: So 1 - z/√(z²+R²) ≈ 1 - (1 - R²/2z²) = R²/2z².
Step 3: E ≈ (σ/2ε₀)(R²/2z²) = σπR²/(4πε₀z²) = Q/(4πε₀z²) where Q = σπR².
Step 4: Both forms B and C are equivalent, representing the point charge limit.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A charge Q is distributed uniformly throughout a sphere of radius R. The electrostatic self-energy of this configuration is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Energy U = (ε₀/2)∫E²dV. Inside sphere (r < R): E = Qr/(4πε₀R³). Outside: E = Q/(4πε₀r²).
Step 2: U = (ε₀/2)[∫₀ᴿ (Qr/4πε₀R³)²4πr²dr + ∫ᴿ^∞ (Q/4πε₀r²)²4πr²dr].
Step 3: = (Q²/8πε₀)[∫₀ᴿ r⁴/R⁶ dr + ∫ᴿ^∞ r⁻² dr] = (Q²/8πε₀)[1/5R + 1/R] = (Q²/8πε₀)(6/5R) = 3Q²/(20πε₀R).
Step 4: This is the work needed to assemble the charged sphere.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two concentric spherical shells of radii a and b (a < b) carry charges Q_a and Q_b. The potential difference V_a - V_b is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Potential at r = a: V_a = (1/4πε₀)[Q_a/a + Q_b/b].
Step 2: Potential at r = b: V_b = (1/4πε₀)[Q_a/b + Q_b/b] = (Q_a + Q_b)/(4πε₀b).
Step 3: V_a - V_b = (1/4πε₀)[Q_a/a + Q_b/b - Q_a/b - Q_b/b] = (Q_a/4πε₀)(1/a - 1/b).
Step 4: The outer charge Q_b doesn't contribute to potential difference (same potential at both radii).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A dipole with moment p is placed in a uniform electric field E. The minimum work required to rotate it from stable equilibrium to θ = 180° is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Potential energy U = -p·E = -pEcosθ.
Step 2: Stable equilibrium: θ = 0, U = -pE.
Step 3: At θ = 180°: U = -pE(-1) = +pE.
Step 4: Work required = ΔU = pE - (-pE) = 2pE. This is the energy barrier for dipole flip.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A parallel plate capacitor with plate area A and separation d is half-filled with dielectric (constant K) of thickness d/2. The capacitance is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: This is series combination: air gap (d/2, ε₀) and dielectric (d/2, Kε₀).
Step 2: C_air = ε₀A/(d/2) = 2ε₀A/d. C_diel = 2Kε₀A/d.
Step 3: Series: 1/C = 1/C_air + 1/C_diel = d/(2ε₀A) + d/(2Kε₀A) = (d/2ε₀A)(1 + 1/K) = (d/2ε₀A)(K+1)/K.
Step 4: C = (2ε₀A/d) × K/(K+1) = (ε₀A/d) × 2K/(K+1).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A point charge q is placed at distance a from an infinite grounded conducting plane. The force on the charge is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Method of images: replace plane with image charge -q at distance a behind plane.
Step 2: Force on real charge = attraction to image charge: F = q²/(4πε₀(2a)²) = q²/(16πε₀a²).
Step 3: Direction is toward the image, i.e., toward the plane.
Step 4: This is the attractive force between charge and induced negative charge on plane.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A capacitor C is charged to voltage V and then connected to an identical uncharged capacitor. The final energy is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Initial charge Q = CV, initial energy U_i = ½CV².
Step 2: When connected, charge redistributes. Total capacitance = 2C (parallel).
Step 3: Final voltage V_f = Q/(2C) = CV/(2C) = V/2.
Step 4: Final energy U_f = ½(2C)(V/2)² = C(V²/4) = ¼CV². Energy is lost (½ → ¼) due to sparking/resistance during charge redistribution.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The electric field in a region is E = axî where a is constant. The charge density in the region is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Gauss's law in differential form: ∇·E = ρ/ε₀.
Step 2: ∇·E = ∂E_x/∂x + ∂E_y/∂y + ∂E_z/∂z = ∂(ax)/∂x = a.
Step 3: Therefore ρ = ε₀(∇·E) = aε₀.
Step 4: The charge density is uniform (constant) throughout the region, despite the field varying linearly with x.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A conducting sphere of radius R has charge Q. A point charge q is brought from infinity to distance 2R from center. The work done by external agent is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Outside a charged conducting sphere, the electric field is identical to that of a point charge Q located at its center.
Step 2: The potential at distance r = 2R is V = Q/(4πε₀(2R)) = Q/(8πε₀R).
Step 3: Work done in bringing charge q from infinity is W = qV.
Step 4: Therefore W = qQ/(8πε₀R). No additional q² term appears since the sphere already has fixed charge Q.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A dielectric slab of thickness t is inserted between plates of capacitor (separation d, area A). The capacitance increases by factor:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Series combination: air gap (d-t) and dielectric (t).
Step 2: C_air = ε₀A/(d-t), C_diel = Kε₀A/t.
Step 3: 1/C = (d-t)/(ε₀A) + t/(Kε₀A) = [K(d-t) + t]/(Kε₀A).
Step 4: C = Kε₀A/[K(d-t) + t] = ε₀A/[d - t + t/K]. Original C₀ = ε₀A/d. Ratio: C/C₀ = d/[d-t+t/K].

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two charges +4q and -q are placed at x = 0 and x = d. The neutral point (zero field) is at:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Let neutral point be at x > d (to the right of both charges, where fields can oppose).
Step 2: Field from +4q: 4q/(4πε₀x²) to right. Field from -q: q/(4πε₀(x-d)²) to left (toward -q).
Step 3: For zero field: 4/x² = 1/(x-d)² → 2/x = 1/(x-d) → 2(x-d) = x → 2x - 2d = x → x = 2d.
Step 4: At x = 2d: distance to +4q is 2d, to -q is d. Field ratio (4/(2d)²)/(1/d²) = 4/4 = 1. Fields cancel.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question:
Passage: A spherical capacitor consists of an inner sphere of radius a and an outer concentric shell of radius b (b > a). The space between them is filled with a dielectric whose relative permittivity varies as K(r) = K0 (r/a), where r is the radial distance from the center.

Question: The capacitance of the capacitor is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Using Gauss's law in dielectric: D = Q/(4πr²).
Step 2: Electric field E = D/(ε0K(r)) = Q/(4πr²ε0K0(r/a)) = Qa/(4πε0K0 r³).
Step 3: Potential difference V = ∫ₐᵇ E dr = Qa/(4πε0K0) ∫ₐᵇ r⁻³ dr.
Step 4: ∫ r⁻³ dr = −1/(2r²). Evaluating from a to b gives V = Q(b² − a²)/(8πε0K0 a b²).
Step 5: Capacitance C = Q/V = 8πε0K0 a b² / (b² − a²).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Using the same spherical capacitor with dielectric K(r) = K0 (r/a), the energy stored when charge Q is placed on it is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Energy stored in a capacitor is U = Q²/(2C).
Step 2: From previous result, C = 8πε₀K₀ a b²/(b² − a²).
Step 3: Substituting gives U = Q²(b² − a²)/(16πε₀K₀ a b²).
Step 4: The logarithmic form applies only when K ∝ a/r, not when K ∝ r/a.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A dipole p is placed at distance r from a point charge q on the dipole axis. The force on the dipole is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Field from charge q at distance r: E = q/(4πε₀r²).
Step 2: Field gradient dE/dr = -2q/(4πε₀r³) = -q/(2πε₀r³).
Step 3: Force on dipole: F = p(dE/dr) = p × q/(2πε₀r³) = qp/(2πε₀r³).
Step 4: The force is attractive if p points toward q (negative charge end closer), repulsive otherwise. Magnitude is qp/(2πε₀r³).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A parallel plate capacitor is charged and disconnected from battery. A dielectric slab is inserted. Which quantity remains constant?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Disconnected from battery: no path for charge to leave or enter.
Step 2: Therefore charge Q on plates remains constant (conservation of charge).
Step 3: Inserting dielectric increases capacitance C, decreases voltage V = Q/C, decreases field E = V/d, and decreases energy U = Q²/2C.
Step 4: The energy decrease means work is done by the system (dielectric pulled in).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The electric potential in a region is V = 3x² + 2y² - z². The electric field at (1,1,1) is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Electric field E = -∇V = -(∂V/∂x i + ∂V/∂y j + ∂V/∂z k).
Step 2: ∂V/∂x = 6x, ∂V/∂y = 4y, ∂V/∂z = -2z.
Step 3: At (1,1,1): E = -(6(1)i + 4(1)j - 2(1)k) = -(6i + 4j - 2k).
Step 4: The field points in direction of steepest potential decrease.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A charged soap bubble of radius R and surface tension T has excess pressure ΔP = 4T/R (electrostatic effects negligible). If it has charge Q, the additional pressure due to electrostatic repulsion is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: For conducting sphere, electrostatic pressure (outward) = σ²/2ε₀ = (Q/4πR²)²/2ε₀ = Q²/(32π²ε₀R⁴).
Step 2: This is the electrostatic stress on the surface.
Step 3: Both forms A and C express the same quantity, just in different variables.
Step 4: The total excess pressure becomes ΔP_total = 4T/R - Q²/(32π²ε₀R⁴) (electrostatic reduces effective surface tension).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In a Van de Graaff generator, the maximum potential is limited by:
options: The charge capacity of the dome
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Van de Graaff generator accumulates charge on a metal dome.
Step 2: The electric field at surface E = V/R. When E exceeds dielectric strength of surrounding gas (~3 MV/m for air), electrical breakdown occurs.
Step 3: This causes spark discharge, limiting maximum voltage.
Step 4: Operating in high-pressure gas or with larger radius dome allows higher voltages.
